subject: Follow-up: Discovery -> Model-fit ask + prompt sample collection
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@brightsearch.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Jul 2025 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Discovery -> Model-fit ask + prompt sample collection

Hi Elaine — thanks again for the thoughtful conversation earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to act from: 

Summary of needs we heard
- Use case: downstream search result re-ranking and short-form answer generation inside BrightSearch results pages (user queries + first-party click/context).
- Key constraints: strict PII redaction (emails, SSNs), 90th-pct latency SLO < 250ms for generation calls, budget sensitivity for high-volume reranking.
- Success criteria for POC: end-to-end quality (NDCG) lift on rerank + no production-level PII leakage on a 200-sample audit set.

Initial model recommendations (for evaluation)
- Redwood-verified: small/medium quantized open model (gpt-neox-20b-8bit-like) for rerank scoring; larger instruction-tuned variant for answer generation (eval for latency trade-off).
- We'll run the models against your benchmark harness (link below) and share token-cost projections + p95 latency.

Action items I need from BrightSearch
1) Sample prompt bank: please upload ~150–250 representative user queries and the top-k context fragments you send to the model. Include edge cases (short queries, very long context, personal contact info, legal/legalese requests). Use the attached CSV template: prompt_samples_template.csv.
2) Redaction guidance: we need a short note on what you consider sensitive that must be redacted vs. what can be pseudonymized. If you have a policy doc, upload it — we can mirror the redaction rules.
3) Benchmarks access: grant our team access to your benchmark harness folder (we provided a read/write Drive link below) or share a snapshot.

Attachments: prompt_samples_template.csv (csv) — simple columns: sample_id, user_query, context_snippet, expected_behavior_flag (rerank/answer), edgecase_tag
Links: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/BRIGHT/benchmark-harness-v2 (benchmark harness + evaluator)

Timeline proposal
- By Fri 7/11: BrightSearch uploads sample prompts + redaction policy excerpt.
- Week of 7/14: Redwood runs initial model-fit runs, shares model selection + token-cost estimate.
- Week of 7/21: Joint POC (2-week) kickoff if both sides greenlight.

A couple of notes on privacy/regression checks
- We'll prepare an automated regression guard that flags hallucination and privacy regressions against a holdout set you provide. For privacy, our guidance is: replace obvious PII with deterministic tokens (e.g., [EMAIL_HASH:abc123]) rather than deleting user intent. We'll add concrete examples once you share the policy.

If the timeline above works, please upload the CSV and any policy excerpts to the Drive link and reply to this thread so Ben and I can schedule the technical kickoff.

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Solution Architect, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
(attachment: prompt_samples_template.csv)

From: Elaine Park <elaine@brightsearch.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Matt Lewis <matt.lewis@brightsearch.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Discovery -> Model-fit ask + prompt sample collection

Jonas — thanks for the clear recap and timeline. A couple quick items from our side: 

1) Redaction: BrightSearch policy requires removal of full SSNs and bank account numbers; for emails and names we prefer pseudonymization unless the PII is critical to query intent. I'll attach our redaction policy excerpt. (attachment: brightsearch-redaction-policy.pdf)

2) Sample prompts: I'm attaching three example rows inline to show format — we can export ~200 rows by tomorrow: 
- sample_001, "What's the best way to reset my password?", "Search result snippet: 'Reset instructions for user@company.com'", rerank, edgecase:none
- sample_002, "Contest rules for customer-12345", "Snippet includes 'Account: John Doe, john.doe@example.com'", answer, edgecase:contains_email
- sample_003, "Return policy for items over $1,000", "Snippet: 'Order # 99887766'", rerank, edgecase:order_id

3) Clarify scope: We can provide a holdout set of 50 manually reviewed queries with expected NDCG lift targets. We'll upload that as well.

Question: for the pseudonymization approach you suggested, can you confirm whether Redwood hashes emails deterministically so we can re-map for downstream analytics? Also — who should I put on Drive permissions for Redwood?

— Elaine
Elaine Park
Director of Product, BrightSearch
elaine@brightsearch.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@brightsearch.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jul 2025 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Discovery -> Model-fit ask + prompt sample collection

Elaine — quick commercial note from our side: happy to support the POC on the timelines above. To keep the POC scoped we typically cover compute and model-run credits while customers cover data prep and storage. If the POC proceeds to a paid pilot, we'll propose a reserved capacity commit with predictable throughput pricing. 

If you want me to spin up a short SOW/POC SOW draft, I can drop a DocuSign link into this thread once you confirm the scope (#weeks, evaluation metrics).

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@brightsearch.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Matt Lewis <matt.lewis@brightsearch.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jul 2025 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Discovery -> Model-fit ask + prompt sample collection

Perfect — appreciate the quick turn. A few clarifications and concrete redaction examples to make uploads consistent: 

Redaction / pseudonymization examples we prefer (for your CSV upload)
- Emails: replace with [EMAIL_HASH:<first8hex>] where the hash is SHA1 truncated (deterministic). Example: 'john.doe@example.com' -> [EMAIL_HASH:3f8a1b2c].
- Phone numbers: replace digits with [PHONE_REDACTED] unless the digits are required for intent.
- Names: replace full name strings with [PERSON_A], [PERSON_B] only if identity is not required to evaluate intent.
- Order IDs / internal ids: keep if they influence retrieval; if they contain user PII, pseudonymize similarly.

Upload instructions
- Use the attached CSV template (prompt_samples_template.csv). Columns: sample_id, original_query, context, expected_behavior (rerank/answer), edgecase_tag, notes, pii_redacted (yes/no).
- Place files in this Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/BRIGHT/benchmark-harness-v2 and grant edit access to jonas_weber@redwood.ai and ben_carter@redwood.ai.

Model selection & regression checks
- We'll run three candidate models against your sample set and produce: NDCG delta, token-cost estimate, p95 latency. We'll also run a privacy-scan that flags any output containing unsubstituted email patterns or SSN-like tokens.
- If a privacy regression is detected on the holdout set, we'll quarantine the run and notify your team.

Next steps (confirmable in this thread)
- Elaine / Matt: upload CSV + redaction excerpt to Drive by EOD Fri 7/11 (per your note).
- Ben: please prepare a 1-page POC SOW draft and drop DocuSign if BrightSearch confirms scope.
- Jonas: will schedule a 45-min tech kickoff the week of 7/14 once we have the samples.

Thanks — looking forward to running the harness.
Jonas Weber
Solution Architect, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
(attachments: benchmark-harness-v2.md, prompt_samples_template.csv)
